content.text:
I submitted index 134 (Ca 0.22, Cu 0.54, V 0.24) as the best composition. The budget allowed only three merit measurements, and 134 had the highest external quantum efficiency (EQE) of the three:

| Index | Ca / Cu / V | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| **134** | 0.22 / 0.54 / 0.24 | **0.166** |
| 69 | 0.20 / 0.30 / 0.50 | 0.106 |
| 138 | 0.31 / 0.47 / 0.23 | 0.087 |

- **Strategy:** I measured 134 first because it is the most Cu-rich composition in the library, and copper vanadates absorb well at the 2.4 eV illumination.
- **What the other two showed:** the V-rich point (69) came in lower. Adding Ca at high Cu (138) lowered EQE further. That points to the Cu-rich, low-Ca corner, where 134 sits.
- **Not used:** I spent none of the 5 XRD measurements and never read the phase list, which was too large to return. So there's no structural evidence behind the choice.
- **Limitation:** the other 135 compositions were never measured, so the library's true best could be somewhere I didn't test. The nearby Cu-rich compositions 122 and 133 are the most likely candidates to beat 134.
